title: Finance & Legal: Budgeting, Contracts, Procurement, and Revenue Recognition Policy
author: Maya Thompson
body:
Overview:
This document consolidates Redwood Inference's finance and legal operating policies for annual budgeting and forecasting, contracts and legal intake, procurement and vendor management, and revenue recognition and billing. It defines roles, processes, approval thresholds, SLAs, and accounting treatment to ensure consistent execution and compliance with accounting standards (ASC 606) and internal controls.

Purpose and scope:
- Purpose: Provide a single reference for finance, legal, procurement, sales, and engineering stakeholders to reduce cycle times, improve accuracy, and maintain audit readiness.
- Scope: Applies to all Redwood entities and covers: annual budget process, quarterly and rolling forecasts, contract lifecycle management (CLM), vendor procurement and POs, purchase card usage, revenue recognition policies, invoicing, and billing adjustments.

1) Budgeting and forecasting
Summary:
- Annual budget (top-down + bottom-up hybrid) approved by the Board.
- Quarterly re-forecast (rolling 12-month) used for operational planning and cash management.
- Monthly actuals vs. forecast reviews at finance leadership and GTM/engineering partner meetings.

Cadence and deliverables:
1. Annual budget cycle (timeline):
   - July–August: Budget kick-off; guidance issued by Finance (CFO & Head of FP&A).
   - August–September: Department submissions (bottom-up) with supporting headcount and operating plans.
   - October: Finance consolidation, scenario analysis (base/optimistic/conservative).
   - November: Exec review iterations.
   - December: Final budget presented to Board and published.
2. Quarterly re-forecast and rolling 12-month:
   - Due: first week of each quarter.
   - Trigger: material changes in bookings, renewals, or major hiring.
3. Monthly close and variance reporting:
   - Deliverables: P&L, cash forecast, headcount dashboard, and variance commentary by the 7th business day each month.

Ownership and responsibilities:
- CFO: final budget owner and Board presenter.
- Head of FP&A: coordinate submissions, consolidation, scenario modeling, and variance analysis.
- Department heads: submit line-item budgets, hiring plans, and risk notes.
- Revenue Operations: provide bookings and ARR/TCV schedules used in revenue forecasts.

Budgeting standards and guardrails:
- Capital vs. operating classification guidance included in the submission template.
- Headcount must use standardized salary bands and burden rates (benefits, taxes, equity).
- All material (> $250k ARR impact or $500k spend) must include an ROI narrative and risks.

2) Contracts and legal process
Intake and triage:
- All contract requests must be submitted through the Contract Intake portal (Salesforce/CLM).
- Intake metadata required: counterparty legal name, SOW/T&Cs summary, estimated ARR/TCV, term length, renewal/auto-renew flags, requested changes to standard terms.

Standard SLAs:
- NDA (standard): 2 business days.
- Standard SaaS MSA (no deviations from template): 3–5 business days.
- Negotiated MSA (commercial changes): target 7–12 business days.
- Complex enterprise deals / regulated customer: target 15–30 business days (cross-functional review).

Approval matrix and signature authorities:
- Sales Director approval required for discounts between 0–10%.
- VP Sales approval required for discounts 10–25% or contract modifications impacting revenue recognition.
- CFO approval required for discounts > 25%, non-standard billing terms, or multi-year commitments > $5M.
- Legal Counsel must approve non-standard indemnities, data residency changes, or customer-requested audit rights.
- Authorized signatories: CEO, CFO, Head of Legal, and delegated VPs per contract value thresholds (maintained in the Signatory Roster).

Standard contract templates and clauses:
- Templates: NDA, MSA (SaaS), SOW, Professional Services Agreement, Channel Reseller Agreement.
- Key clauses: data processing addendum (DPA), liability caps, IP ownership, termination for convenience, uptime SLA/credits, export controls, and audit rights.
- All templates are maintained in the CLM library and require Legal approval for changes.

Repository and audit trail:
- All fully executed agreements must be uploaded to the CLM and mirrored to the legal secure drive.
- Versioning and redlines retained for audit; retention policy aligns with records retention schedule.

3) Procurement procedures and vendor management
Procurement flow:
1. Vendor selection and quote collection.
2. Procurement intake form in the Vendor Portal (business owner initiates).
3. Legal and Security review for third-party risk (if vendor stores customer data or has network access).
4. PO issuance (Finance generates PO after approvals).
5. Vendor onboarding and payment setup.

Thresholds & approvals:
- Low-value operating purchases (< $5k): department manager approval.
- Medium-value purchases ($5k–$50k): Senior Manager/Director approval.
- High-value purchases (>$50k): VP approval + procurement review.
- Capital purchases over $250k: require CFO and CEO approval and must include capex business case.

Preferred vendors and negotiation:
- Finance maintains a list of preferred vendors (discount schedules, negotiated terms).
- For recurring SaaS vendors, Procurement seeks annual contracts and consolidated billing to reduce overhead.

Purchase orders and P-Card usage:
- P-cards may be used per P-Card policy (up to $5k single transaction) with monthly reconciliation.
- POs required for vendors that bill against a contract or when requested by vendor.

Vendor risk and security checks:
- Vendors with access to customer data or infra require a security questionnaire and, where applicable, SOC2 Type II or equivalent evidence.
- Legal must review standard vendor agreement terms for data processing and liability.

4) Revenue recognition and billing policies (ASC 606 aligned)
Revenue streams covered:
- Hosted API consumption (usage-based).
- Subscription plans (monthly/annual) for Redwood Console and Optimize.
- Dedicated and Private deployment contracts (fixed-fee, term-based, may include implementation SOWs).
- Professional services and implementation fees.

Contract identification and performance obligations:
- Each customer contract is evaluated to identify distinct performance obligations (hosting, professional services, premium support).
- Standalone selling prices (SSP) are established for each performance obligation using observable pricing or allocation methods.

Timing of recognition:
- Subscription revenue: recognized ratably over the contractual period.
- Usage-based revenue: recognized as the service is consumed (measured usage each billing period).
- Implementation/professional services: recognized over time if criteria met (input/output methods) or at a point in time if deliverable is distinct.
- One-time setup fees: typically deferred and recognized over the expected benefit period unless the fee is compensation for a distinct service.

Billing and invoicing practices:
- Standard payment terms: Net 30 from invoice date unless otherwise approved.
- Preferred billing systems: Stripe for self-serve/hosted; Zuora/NetSuite invoicing for enterprise (depending on integration).
- Invoicing cadence: monthly in arrears for usage; monthly or annual in advance for subscriptions per contract.
- Taxes: Sales tax/VAT is collected per customer jurisdiction; Revenue Ops calculates tax obligations with Tax provider integration.

Contract modifications and renewals:
- Change orders: amendments are processed via CLM and evaluated for incremental costs and revenue allocation.
- Renewals: auto-renew behavior is tracked; renewal notices must be issued per contract term and Sales/Customer Success manage commercial terms.

Credits, refunds, and disputes:
- Credits for SLA breaches follow the SLA credit schedule and are applied to the next invoice or as credit memos.
- Refunds are exceptional and require Finance + Sales Director approval.
- Dispute resolution: disputed items flagged in billing system and hold applied until resolution; recurring disputes escalate to Revenue Ops.

Month-end close and accounting treatment:
- Revenue cut-off: all invoices and usage reports must be submitted by the close checklist deadline (2 business days before close).
- Deferred revenue entries created for invoices billed in advance.
- Journal entries for revenue, deferred revenue, and unbilled receivables documented with supporting schedules.
- Revenue reconciliations performed monthly by Revenue Accounting (Revenue Ops + Accounting Manager).

Controls, reporting, and audit readiness:
- Segregation of duties between Sales, Revenue Ops, and Accounting for contract creation, invoicing, and cash collection.
- Quarterly internal reviews of revenue recognition policies and at least annual external audit.
- Maintain evidence: executed contracts, CLM metadata, invoice history, usage reports, and allocation workpapers.

Appendix A — Quick reference tables
1) Approval matrix (summary):
- < $5k: Manager
- $5k–$50k: Director
- $50k–$250k: VP + Procurement
- > $250k: CFO + CEO for capital

2) Contract SLA overview:
- NDA: 2 business days
- Standard MSA: 3–5 business days
- Negotiated MSA: 7–12 business days
- Complex deals: 15–30 business days

Change history and governance:

- Review cadence: Annual by Finance + Legal; interim updates as required for regulatory or accounting standard changes.

- legal-ops@redwood.ai (for contract intake & templates)

This policy is intended to provide consistent guardrails and enable efficient cross-functional execution. Where exceptional circumstances occur, the documented approval matrix and escalation paths must be followed.
